learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding of the principles of operation of modern high-frequency analog front-end architectures.
Knowledge of the parameters characterizing high frequency communication systems.
Knowledge of CAD-assisted analysis methods of high frequency active electronic circuits.
Knowledge of circuit topologies of functional blocks in high frequency systems.
Knowledge of the design methods of functional blocks in use in high frequency systems.
Ability to understand the operation of radio architectures.
Ability to compare different technologies and architectures in relation to application requirements.
Ability to use CAD systems for the design of high frequency circuits.
Ability to understand the development of the layer of art and the generations of new technologies and architectures for high frequency applications.
Ability to logically expose the principles of operation of high frequency electronic subsystems.
Ability to logically expose the correct application of the techniques used for the development of high frequency systems for use in telecommunications.
Ability to independently investigate operating principles and innovative properties of new systems and subsystems for high frequency applications.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to radio frequency systems: evolution of electronics and wireless systems
Basic concepts: noise, sensitivity and nonlinearity concepts in radio systems
Theory of high frequency networks and concepts related to power gain and adaptations
Methods of analysis of non-linear networks and in the envelope domain
Modulators and demodulators: fundamental configurations for balanced mixers and their use in modulators and demodulators
Oscillators and phase coupling rings: fundamental configurations for oscillators and principle of operation of the PLL
Power amplifiers: discussion of the various classes of operation and design techniques
Digital techniques in radios systems for the transmission of digitally modulated signals, characteristic aspects and their impact on the subsystems used
Exercises in CAD Laboratory: design of a class AB amplifier and possible implementation at the Department’s “RF Microwave and Electromagnetism” Laboratory
assessment_rules: Verification of learning skills occurs through an oral exam and description of laboratory activities. Grading ranges from 18 to 30 with Honors (Lode). Failure results from serious conceptual errors, fragmentary understanding, or inability to apply knowledge. Honors is awarded for work distinguished by brilliance and originality.
bibliography: S. A. Maas, Nonlinear Microwave and RF Circuits, 2nd ed., Artech House, 2003.
S. C. Cripps, RF Power Amplifiers for Wireless Communications, 2nd ed., Artech House, 2006.
Lecture notes provided by the teacher.
